title: The modern integer 3SUM conjecture
decision_reason: Explicit bounded-error integer formulation, independent current corroboration, thirteen scope comparisons, duplicate check, separated A53 self-review and technical validation passed. No matching unresolved resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.input: For n>=3, an explicitly listed set S of n distinct signed integers in [-n^3,n^3].
problem_fingerprint.question: Does S contain three pairwise distinct elements a,b,c with a+b=c?
problem_fingerprint.computational_model: One uniform randomized classical word-RAM program with word size Theta(log n), standard word operations and indexed memory access; all computation and input-dependent preprocessing counted.
problem_fingerprint.success: For every valid input, correct yes/no answer with probability at least 2/3 over internal randomness.
problem_fingerprint.complexity_target: No fixed epsilon>0 and such algorithm have worst-case expected running time O(n^(2-epsilon)) as n tends to infinity.
problem_fingerprint.encoding: Each signed integer occupies O(log n) bits; n is the number of input integers. No real-number oracle, free input-dependent preprocessing or advice depending on n.
problem_fingerprint.canonical_scope: One integer-3SUM family, including the standard three-set/zero-sum formulations. Neither arbitrary k nor restricted-input/space-query variants are separate additions.
problem_fingerprint.old_conjecture_distinction: A strict Omega(n^2) bound is not asserted; logarithmic savings are compatible with the fixed-power hardness target.

statement_sources.locator: Section 1.1, 3SUM definition; Section 2 opening and 2.1, randomized word-RAM conventions and 3SUM conjecture.
Section 2.1, Definition 2.1, Hypothesis 2.2 and variant-equivalence paragraph.

independently_authored_corroboration.independence: Both author teams are disjoint from Ball–Rosen–Sabin–Vasudevan and Jin–Xu; their July and August 2026 introductions retain the fixed-power 3SUM hypothesis.
independently_authored_corroboration.scope: The tripartite formulation is connected to the displayed one-set convention in JX23 and GP14; no real/integer machine-model equivalence is assumed.

nearest_existing.comparison: Complex scalar arithmetic for dense matrix products and exponent two; not a bounded-word integer decision problem or the same lower-bound assertion.
Deterministic two-party communication with free local computation; not total randomized machine time on a single explicit input.
Derandomizing identity testing for compact polynomial circuits; not an exponent lower bound for a fixed additive relation on an explicit set.

duplicate_check.result: No equivalent active or accepted entry located. Reductions to graph and geometric problems are disclosed rather than treated as logical independence.

second_review.arrangement: Primary-agent research followed by a clearly separated adversarial self-pass; no independent agent or human review.
issues_found: The original expected-time source has a zero-error convention, unlike the bounded-error draft.
Additional subquadratic algorithm titles included Sopin, algebraic 3SUM and Freund.
Decision-tree depth, preprocessing cost, word width and input promises could be confused with uniform total running time.
issues_resolved: Checked BRSV17 full §2 convention giving success 2/3 on every input; separated it from P10 and explained the expected-time normalization.

Read complete S15 Theorem 2/proof and BCILOS17 model/theorem statements. For subscription-restricted F17, used the exact full-text scholarly restatement C19 §1 and publisher formula, retaining the access limit.
Kept all preprocessing, finite integer encoding and logarithmic word width explicit; compared current 2026 theorems hypothesis by hypothesis.
second_review.quantifier_checks: One uniform classical algorithm, all n>=3 and every valid distinct-element input; fixed positive exponent improvement; probability at least 2/3 per input; maximum over inputs of expected steps. No advice, promised additive structure, or supplied data structure.
second_review.application_check: Conditional complexity links to exact combinatorial, dynamic graph and geometric computation; foundational worst-case relevance only.
second_review.duplicate_check: Fresh alias search over active pages, metadata and all candidate records found no equivalent problem. Full nearest statements 033, 301 and 321 were reread; model differences recorded.
second_review.search_limit: No independent proof certification. Original F17 journal proof inaccessible, with exact bound corroborated in accessible primary research. GP14 and JX23 cited preprints were read; full journal versions were not line-compared.

normalization_checks.expected_time: Within bounded-error algorithms, a constant-factor timeout followed by constant amplification converts worst-case expected time to a bounded running time with success 2/3 and the same fixed-power exponent. This is not an equivalence between zero-error and bounded-error hardness. P10 is explicitly separated from BRSV17.
normalization_checks.input_convention: The displayed distinct-elements, a+b=c convention follows BRSV17 verbatim in mathematical scope. JX23 explicitly discusses standard variant equivalence; it is not inferred from similar titles.
normalization_checks.small_universe: Fast convolution with cost depending on the integer universe does not automatically yield a fixed-power speedup when its radius is n^3.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Worst-case assumptions imply average-case hardness for related functions.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: A conditional transfer establishes neither this base conjecture nor its refutation.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Hardness for Sidon instances follows from the 3SUM hypothesis; reductions can remove additive structure.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Conditional hardness and algorithms on low-doubling inputs supply no unconditional general fixed-power algorithm.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: For 0<=epsilon<=1/2, preprocessing time ~O(n^2), space ~O(n^(2-2epsilon/3)), query time ~O(n^(3/2+epsilon)).
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The displayed query saving excludes input-dependent preprocessing, which this candidate counts.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Decision-tree depth O(n^(3/2)*sqrt(log n)); deterministic and randomized uniform algorithms save logarithmic factors.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The former counts queries rather than total uniform time; the latter do not give n^(2-epsilon) for any fixed positive epsilon.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A set covered by n^(1-delta) boxes of volume n in fixed dimension permits expected n^(2-Omega(delta)) time.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: For dimension one and fixed delta>0 the short-interval covering promise need not hold for an arbitrary set in [-n^3,n^3].

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Preprocessing ~O(n^2), space ~O(n^max(2-epsilon,11/6-epsilon/3)), queries ~O(n^(3/2+epsilon)); adaptive queries supported.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: Improved storage and query robustness retain the quadratic preprocessing term.
Indexing counts an already-built data structure, whereas this decision problem counts the full computation.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Triangle bounds improve with word width; four-cycle results have larger-word or dense-graph conditions.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: At w=Theta(log n), the relevant improvements retain their polynomial exponents. The other task/promise conditions do not supply a general integer-3SUM solver.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Expected-time hardness is posed for zero-error algorithms.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: This does not alone justify bounded-error hardness. The latter is explicitly sourced to BRSV17; timeout plus amplification only normalizes bounded-error expected versus bounded time.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Total subquadratic runtime depends on the number of surviving tuples after filtering.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: No all-input bound at the required exponent is stated. Lemma 4 only bounds Algorithm 1, not all of Algorithm 2.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Nonuniform decision-tree depth O(n^(12/7+epsilon)); uniform real-RAM time O(n^2*(log log n)^(3/2)/sqrt(log n)).
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The fixed exponent saving belongs to a model with free auxiliary computation; the uniform algorithm has only logarithmic savings.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Deterministic real-RAM time O(n^2*poly(log w)/(w log n)), with logarithmic-size words permitted.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: At the candidate word width this is n^(2-o(1)), preserving the conjectured fixed-power barrier.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Publisher abstract; accessible full-text restatement C19 §1, p. 7:2
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Deterministic O(n^2*log log n/log n) for 3SUM.
resolution_comparisons.mismatch: The improvement is logarithmic. Original proof inaccessible; exact bound is independently restated in full scholarly text, with no conflicting claim located.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Subquadratic space and sublinear query time for 3SUM indexing, allowing unlimited preprocessing time.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: This refutes the strong indexing conjecture, not the total-time integer 3SUM conjecture. The present entry counts preprocessing on each input.
